title: Tech Sells Off as Treasuries Rally: Where I'd Put Cash
intro: The Nasdaq lost 2.6% on Thursday while the Dow edged higher and Treasury prices rallied. This is a rotation away from expensive AI exposure, not a market-wide collapse. With oil still high and AI borrowing costs under scrutiny, Treasury duration, cash-rich fertiliser and quality earnings deserve more attention than blind technology dip-buying.

sections.label: What Actually Changed
sections.text: A concentrated technology sell-off met a Treasury safe-haven bid; breadth is not uniformly weak.
paragraphs: At Thursday's close, SPY fell 1.18% and QQQ fell 2.86%. Semiconductor ETF SMH fell 5.99%, while the equal-weight S&P ETF RSP rose 0.73%, consumer staples ETF XLP gained 3.31% and healthcare ETF XLV gained 1.32%. This is an important rotation rather than index-only panic.

The ten-year Treasury dipped under 5% while Meta fell 6.98%, Micron fell 6.26%, GE Vernova fell 10.64%, and Eaton fell 6.33%. These are 22 October completed US closing prices, not earnings estimates. Match the bond rally against HY/IG spreads before calling it broad credit contagion.

Brent/oil inflation and French sovereign risk remain material. A Treasury flight to safety can coexist with rising inflation expectations; do not infer an automatic Fed rate cut from lower nominal yields.

sections.label: The Bond Decision — Buy Duration, but Choose It Carefully
sections.text: VGIT first; IEF for more duration; TLT smaller and conditional.
paragraphs: VGIT closed at $57.45 with a Vanguard-reported duration of roughly 4.8–4.9 years and a 0.03% fee. IEF closed at $91.20 and provides longer 7–10-year exposure. Either can be an initial Treasury allocation; owning both is not true diversification because their main driver is US interest rates.

TLT closed at $81.74 after a 1.87% jump. iShares reports an effective duration of 14.79 years and a 30-day SEC yield of 5.41% as of 16 October. A 0.50 percentage-point parallel yield increase could imply roughly 7.4% mark-to-market price loss before coupons and convexity. Treat TLT as a small satellite, not safe cash.

SGOV remains suitable for USD liquidity and dry powder. An individual Treasury maturing on a chosen date can make more sense if the actual objective is guaranteed principal at maturity, rather than a mark-to-market bond-price trade. MYR/USD exposure, taxes and trading costs still matter.

sections.label: Where the Real Earnings Are
sections.text: Avoid equating falling share prices with failing business fundamentals.
paragraphs: TSMC's 15 October Q3 issuer report showed $46.72bn US-dollar revenue, 66.4% gross margin, 58.7% operating margin and Q4 revenue guidance of $52.3–54.3bn. The stock still fell 4.52% on 22 October. That is valuation and factor repricing to investigate, not proof that chip orders disappeared.

Meta's Q3 revenue reached $64.60bn and operating cash flow $32.79bn, while company-wide free cash flow was negative $2.12bn after massive capex. Its 2026 capex range is $135–145bn, narrowed from $130–145bn; a large legal charge also distorted operating earnings. Credit-sensitive customers are more vulnerable than cash-rich hyperscalers.

CF Industries generated $1.34bn H1 net earnings and $1.82bn trailing free cash flow according to the issuer. A provisional same-listed vendor screen gives 8.44x trailing earnings and 9.28x trailing price/free cash flow. The next test is North American natural-gas cost and the 4 November Q3 release, not simply whether oil rises.

sections.label: What I Would Buy and Sell
sections.text: Direct investment instructions, with separate no-order source and readiness checks.
paragraphs: BUY CANDIDATES: a staged VGIT or IEF starter; SGOV for uncommitted cash; a smaller TLT position only if long-end yields and loss budget justify it; CF as the first cash-producing non-AI equity research purchase after a fresh Friday quote.

HOLD or WAIT: XOM as existing core energy; TTWO pending launch evidence; TSM pending tech breadth stabilisation; GEV until 28 October Q3; NEM until its Q3 release is read; GRAB pending Atome/credit and normalized cash. Do not blindly chase a one-day defensive sector rally.

SELL/TRIM REVIEWS: DAYANG is the highest priority for capital recycling because operating results weakened; TSLA merits a trim review after earnings and the 22 October fall; consider reducing YTLPOWR only if verified parent-plus-warrant exposure breaches the user's risk cap. Do not place a trade on the unidentified 6742UW instrument until its exact terms are matched.

sections.label: Next Tests
sections.text: Source coverage remains partial and determines whether these candidates become actual orders.
paragraphs: Obtain official dated 22 October UST nominal and TIPS closes, current HY/IG OAS, bond auctions, DXY/JXY, USDJPY and 20/30-year yield confirmation. Match time and instrument; an equity decline alone is not a Treasury entry trigger.

Read Newmont's Q3 issuer report once independently accessible, GE Vernova's 28 October earnings, CF Industries' 4 November Q3, and the 27–28 October Fed decision. Re-check USD/MYR exposure and Malaysian broker quotes before updating actual orders.

Creator videos remain hypothesis discovery only. The 21 October Mark Malek podcast argues Japanese capital repatriation could pressure Treasuries; its claim that Japanese investors are specifically dumping US Treasuries is not established by all-foreign-bond-sales data. Cross-check Treasury TIC and Japan's Ministry of Finance rather than trade from the transcript.

verdict: Decision: BUY CANDIDATE in staged VGIT or IEF and, where risk budget allows, a small TLT satellite; keep SGOV for liquidity. CF is the leading independently cash-supported equity buy study. SELL/RECYCLE review DAYANG; TRIM review TSLA subject to actual position risk; HOLD XOM. No orders executed. Confirm Friday quotes, USD/MYR, broker access, tax and current issuer evidence before sizing.

introParagraphs: The Nasdaq fell 2.6% to 26,008.86 on 22 October, while the S&P 500 lost 1.2% and the Dow finished slightly higher. The difference matters: investors were not selling everything, but reducing exposure to expensive technology and AI infrastructure.

Treasury prices rose as the ten-year yield fell below 5% intraday. TLT gained 1.87% to $81.74 and IEF rose 1.08% to $91.20. Bond buying is consistent with a growth or financing scare, but persistently expensive oil could revive inflation pressure and make long-duration bonds volatile.

Power Stack can still buy. My first duration study is VGIT at $57.45 (lower interest-rate sensitivity), followed by IEF; TLT is a smaller tactical satellite. CF Industries at $118.56 is the first non-AI equity entry study on cash, valuation and nitrogen fundamentals. These are candidates for staged, limited entries, not unsized orders.
